name: time_scaling
description: Does the DeepSets agent's advantage grow, shrink or hold as the per-turn time budget moves? DeepSetsBotExp vs SakkirinaScaled at per-turn budgets of 2, 5, 10, 20 and (optionally) 30 seconds, with the SAME scale applied to BOTH sides at every budget, 400 games each.
_which_agent: THIS CONFIG MEASURES THE BLEND AGENT, NOT THE NETWORK-ONLY ONE. SOT_ALPHA0 is now written out as 0.7 in every row. That is a no-op: 0.7 is DeepSetsBotExp's built-in default (ALPHA_START), so the rows behave exactly as they did when the variable was absent, and results from the completed run remain valid. It is spelled out because a config that relied on the default did not say anywhere which of the two agents it measured, and the write-up needs that. DeepSetsBotExp at alpha0=0.7 is DeepSetsBlendBot, the 1st-place submission; at alpha0=0 it is DeepSetsBot. So time_scaling's 10s row is the same agent configuration as alpha_sweep's alpha0_0.7 row (modulo --timeout 12 here against 10 there), while BOTH equal_effort configs run alpha0=0 and are therefore measuring a different agent -- do not read a time-scaling row and an equal-effort row as the same agent under two conditions.
_budget_note: Both agents derive their per-turn budget the same way: TurnTimeout = 9.8s * scale and per-move cap = 0.65s * scale. So scale = budget/10 gives a self-imposed cap of 0.98*budget, which is the same 2% margin under the engine clock that the submitted agents use at the stock 10s setting. SOT_TIME_SCALE drives DeepSetsBotExp, SOT_BASELINE_TIME_SCALE drives SakkirinaScaled; they are set to the same number in every row, which is the whole point of the experiment.
_timeout_note: Engine --timeout is budget + 2s, not budget. The engine clock is a per-TURN budget accumulated across moves, and a turn that legitimately spends its whole allowance would otherwise land right on the boundary and be scored TURN_TIMEOUT -- i.e. the tightest budgets would look like the worst agents, for a reason that has nothing to do with play. The margin is why the aggregator reports timeouts separately: if they are not near zero here, the margin is too small and the row's win rate is not a measurement of anything. NOTE this makes the 10s row NOT directly comparable to legacy_paper_benchmark.json, which used --timeout 10 with no margin.

matchups.label: budget_02s
matchups.note: Bot-side cap 1.96s/turn. The shallowest search in the config -- watch the disqualification column, since a shallower tree makes the no-isomorphic-match fallback fire more often.

matchups.label: budget_10s
matchups.note: Stock timing on both sides: bot-side cap 9.8s, exactly what the submitted agents and stock SakkirinaSolo use. The reference row.

matchups.label: budget_30s
matchups.note: OPTIONAL, and the most expensive row by far -- roughly 3x the wall clock of the 10s row for the same 400 games. Skip it by simply not submitting its task-id range (--dry-run prints the range); it is last in the config so leaving it out changes no other row's task ids.
